abstracts.abstract: We propose a novel information-theoretic paradigm for knowledge discovery in high-dimensional datasets that fundamentally reinterprets the learning process as an optimal compression problem. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that optimize predictive accuracy directly, our framework introduces the concept of minimal sufficient statistics within the data mining context, establishing a theoretical bridge between information theory and pattern recognition. The core innovation lies in our formulation of learning as a lossy compression problem where the compression rate is dynamically determined by the intrinsic data structure. We derive new theoretical bounds on the generalization error that are tighter than existing VC-dimension-based guarantees, particularly for overparameterized models. Our analysis reveals fundamental connections between the information bottleneck principle and statistical consistency in clustering tasks. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed paradigm achieves competitive classification performance while providing theoretically grounded interpretability guarantees. This work establishes a new theoretical foundation for intelligent data analysis that unifies supervised and unsupervised learning under a common information-theoretic framework.

Feature selection remains a critical challenge in machine learning, particularly for high-dimensional data. This paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of filter-based feature selection methods and proposes a significant improvement to the conditional mutual information framework. We first identify a fundamental limitation in existing conditional mutual information estimators, demonstrating that they systematically underestimate feature relevance in the presence of complex feature dependencies. Building upon this analysis, we introduce a novel theoretical framework that accounts for higher-order feature interactions through a principled expansion of conditional entropy terms. We prove that our proposed relevance measure satisfies the necessary conditions for optimal feature subset selection under the Markov blanket framework. The theoretical analysis is complemented by an efficient algorithm with provable approximation guarantees. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate our theoretical findings, showing improvements of 3-8% in classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art feature selection methods. Our analysis provides new insights into the relationship between feature redundancy and complementarity in intelligent data analysis.

We present a novel system architecture for large-scale anomaly detection in streaming data that fundamentally reimagines the detection pipeline for modern big data analytics requirements. The proposed system introduces a hierarchical processing paradigm that decomposes the anomaly detection problem across three distinct levels: raw data preprocessing, temporal pattern extraction, and contextual anomaly scoring. At the core of our design is a novel adaptive windowing mechanism that dynamically adjusts to concept drift in data streams, eliminating the need for manual parameter tuning. The system employs a distributed computing architecture that enables horizontal scaling across commodity hardware while maintaining detection accuracy. We introduce a novel lightweight neural network module specifically designed for resource-constrained edge deployment, enabling real-time anomaly detection with minimal latency. The preprocessing module implements a streaming version of our proposed intelligent data analysis pipeline that handles missing values and noise in online settings. Experimental evaluation on multiple streaming datasets demonstrates that the system achieves sub-millisecond detection latency while maintaining detection accuracy comparable to batch processing methods, representing a paradigm shift in practical anomaly detection deployment.

We present an enhanced system for multi-dimensional time series classification that significantly improves upon existing intelligent data analysis pipelines. The system integrates several key innovations: an advanced data preprocessing module that handles heterogeneous data types and temporal misalignment through a novel dynamic time warping variant with learned alignment kernels. For predictive analytics, we design a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines convolutional layers for local pattern recognition with recurrent components for capturing long-range temporal dependencies. A significant system improvement is our proposed attention-based mechanism that automatically identifies and visualizes the most discriminative temporal segments, enhancing model interpretability. The feature selection component employs a wrapper approach using our novel importance metric that considers both predictive relevance and temporal stability. Extensive evaluation on benchmark time series datasets demonstrates that the system achieves state-of-the-art classification performance while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for practical deployment. The system's modular architecture enables flexible configuration for different application scenarios in pattern recognition and knowledge discovery.
